chapters.1.lds: Why does promised relief lead into prayer for continued good work?
chapters.1.summary: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy write again to the Thessalonians. They thank God that the readers’ faith grows and their love increases. They boast of the readers’ endurance in persecutions. They say God will repay the afflicters and give relief to the afflicted. That will happen when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his angels. Those who do not obey the good news will be punished. He will be glorified in his saints on that day. The writers pray that God will count the readers worthy of their calling.
chapters.2.lds: The selected Church lesson applies falling away to the Great Apostasy before Christ's return. Why can a message claimed to come from the teachers still require testing?
chapters.2.summary: Paul asks them not to be shaken by a letter said to be his. Such a message says the day of the Lord has already come. That day will not come before the rebellion and the man of sin. That man will sit in God’s temple and claim to be God. Something now restrains him. The Lord Jesus will destroy him by the breath of his mouth. Those who refused to love the truth will be deceived. Paul thanks God for choosing the readers and tells them to stand firm.
chapters.3.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches useful work for oneself and people in need. How does treating the person as a brother limit the aim of separation?
chapters.3.summary: Paul asks for prayer that the Lord’s word will spread quickly. The Lord is faithful and will guard them. He commands them to withdraw from any brother who refuses to work. He worked night and day and ate no one’s bread for free. He gave the rule that one who will not work should not eat. Some are busybodies and should work quietly. Anyone who ignores this letter should be noted and avoided. Paul signs with his own hand.
